title: C++ - Advanced weird overloads[()]
description:
In C++, we have somthing called _functors_. A functor is a class that behaves like a function. To do this; we use the `()` overload. Yes, you are not going insane: Those are parenthesis.


---

## Signature

```cpp
<anything> operator( )(<arglist>) {
    ...
}
```
Honestly, rather simple. The purpose of functors is for a function to have a continuous state, which in a language like python you would use generators or closures for.


---
## Assignment:
Finish the operator( ) function: It should take a `char`(the operator) and a `int`(the value). It should switch on operator, and on `+`, `+=` the value to acc, for `-` `-=`, `*` `*=`, `/` `/=`, and for `=` assign acc the value.
